Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard bases. Let $X$ be the stable locus in the complex ADHM equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, where $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$, and stability means that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$. The action $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ of $GL(V)$ on $X$ is free and proper. Its orbit quotient with quotient topology is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension $2kN$, with tangent space $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$ for the infinitesimal ADHM deformation maps.

For $k>0$, a word frame $C(x)$ is a matrix whose columns are $k$ fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard framing basis vectors. The opens $U_C=\{x:\det C(x)\ne0\}$ cover $X$; words of length at most $k-1$ suffice. Each slice $S_C=\{x\in U_C:C(x)=I_V\}$ gives quotient coordinates, with $GL(V)\times S_C\to U_C$ a biholomorphism. Slice changes are holomorphic, in fact given by matrix inversion and polynomial operations on their domains. The quotient is also a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite $T$-invariant affine atlas of these slices, and the map from $X$ is a geometric quotient in the regular-function sense.

Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, with $h$ acting on the $\alpha$th standard framing vector by $e_\alpha^{-1}$. This descends to a smooth holomorphic action. At any fixed quotient point represented by $x$, there is a unique $g(t)\in GL(V)$ with $t\cdot x=g(t)\cdot x$. If column $\ell$ of $C(x)$ uses framing color $\alpha_\ell$ and contains $a_\ell,b_\ell$ letters $B_1,B_2$, then

$$g(t)=C(x)\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})C(x)^{-1}.$$

Thus the lift is a smooth character representation, without assuming Zariski density or a GIT linearization theorem. For $k=0$ the quotient is a point and these matrices and tangent spaces have their empty-dimensional interpretations. No correspondence with a real moment-map quotient, sheaf moduli or ASD connections is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a finite-type group scheme of multiplicative type over $k$ ([[def-group-of-multiplicative-type-and-torus]]). Then every rational representation of $G$ ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]) is a direct sum of simple representations, and the simple representations are classified by the $\Gamma_k$-orbits of the character group $X^*(G)$: $G$ is linearly reductive.

Assume the Axiom of Choice where the geometric suppliers of the named items use it. Let $G$ be a linearly reductive affine group variety over $k$ acting on a smooth variety $X$. Then the fixed-point subscheme $X^G$ is smooth (Milne, Ch. 13); if $S\subseteq G(k)$ is Zariski-dense then $X^S=X^G$ and both are smooth (13.5-13.7); if $k$ is algebraically closed and $g\in G(k)$ is semisimple, then the closure of the subgroup generated by $g$ is linearly reductive and $X^g=X^{G_0}$ is smooth (13.8). In particular, if a linearly reductive group $H$ acts on a smooth algebraic group $G$, then the fixed subgroup $G^H$ is smooth; when $H\subseteq G$ acts by conjugation this is $C_G(H)$ (13.9), and for a subgroup $H\subseteq G$ of multiplicative type the centralizer $C_G(H)$ and normalizer $N_G(H)$ are smooth, with no smoothness assumption on $H$. If $H$ is smooth, its geometric points are schematically dense, and these are also the unique smooth closed subgroup schemes whose geometric points are the centralizer and normalizer of $H(k^{\mathrm a})$ (13.10-13.11). The pointwise identification is not asserted for nonsmooth $H$: for $H=\mu_p$ embedded by $t\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(t,1)$ in $\mathrm{GL}_2$ in characteristic $p$, $H(k^{\mathrm a})=1$ but $C_G(H)$ is the diagonal torus.

Let $k$ be any field, let $n\geq0$ be finite, let $I$ be an ideal of
$k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, and put
$$X=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/I).$$
Let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in X(k)$, and let
$f_1,\ldots,f_r$ be any finite generating list of the actual ideal $I$.
Then the coordinate-velocity map gives a canonical $k$-linear isomorphism
$$T_aX\cong\ker\!\left(J_{(f_1,\ldots,f_r)}(a):k^n\longrightarrow k^r\right).$$
The kernel is independent of the chosen finite generating list of $I$. No
reducedness, perfectness, or characteristic hypothesis is needed. Finiteness of
the list is available for every finite $n$ by the finite-variable polynomial
Noetherian result cited below.

derivations.claim: The infinitesimal $GL(V)$ action and the derivative of the complex ADHM equation form the complex $$C^0=\operatorname{End}(V)\xrightarrow{d_0}C^1=\operatorname{End}(V)t_1\oplus\operatorname{End}(V)t_2\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)t_1t_2\xrightarrow{d_1}C^2=\operatorname{End}(V)t_1t_2,$$ where $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$ and $d_1(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)=[\dot B_1,B_2]+[B_1,\dot B_2]+\dot I J+I\dot J$. Expanding gives $d_1d_0(\xi)=[\xi,[B_1,B_2]+IJ]=0$, so this is a complex.

If $d_0(\xi)=0$, then $\xi$ commutes with both $B_i$ and $\xi I=0$. Therefore $\xi B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)=B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}\xi I(w)=0$ for every word and $w$. Stability says those vectors span $V$, hence $\xi=0$ and $d_0$ is injective.

To show $d_1$ is onto, use the nondegenerate trace pairing on $\operatorname{End}(V)$. If $\Theta$ annihilates its image, variation of $\dot J$ gives $\Theta I=0$, and variations of $\dot B_1,\dot B_2$ give $[\Theta,B_1]=[\Theta,B_2]=0$. The same word calculation as in step 2.1 then gives $\Theta=0$. Thus the annihilator of $\operatorname{im}d_1$ is zero, so $d_1$ is surjective.

Apply [F3] to the displayed equation and stability condition. Its proof uses the declared holomorphic implicit-function supplier, proves properness by word-frame bounds on both the gauge transformation and its inverse, and constructs holomorphic quotient charts. Thus the quotient here is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold, with tangent $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$ and complex dimension $2kN$. For $k=0$ the quotient is a point. This is the stable complex quotient; no real moment-map or sheaf/ASD identification is inferred.

At a $T$-fixed quotient point represented by $x$, [F3] gives the unique gauge lift $g(t)=C(x)\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})C(x)^{-1}$ from a standard-framing word basis. This is a smooth representation of the compact torus itself. The fixed-orbit equations give $g(t)I(w_\alpha)=e_\alpha I(w_\alpha)$ and $g(t)B_i=t_iB_i g(t)$, so all weights generated by stability have the form $e_\alpha t_1^it_2^j$ with $i,j\ge0$. Under $t_1t_2hJ=Jg(t)^{-1}$, a nonzero component from a $V$-weight $\chi$ to the $\beta$th framing line requires $\chi=e_\beta t_1^{-1}t_2^{-1}$. Distinct integer characters on the compact torus cannot satisfy this equality with any generated weight, so $J=0$. The moment equation then gives $[B_1,B_2]=0$. No Zariski-density or algebraic lifting assertion is used.

For each framing line, the commuting pair $B_1,B_2$ makes its cyclic span a quotient of $\mathbb C[x,y]$, with $x,y$ acting by $B_1,B_2$. The torus weights $e_\alpha t_1^i t_2^j$ are distinct between colors and between monomials, so the kernel is a monomial ideal. Its standard monomials form a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$, hence a Young diagram $Y_\alpha$. Stability says the cyclic spans together exhaust $V$, so $\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|=\dim V=k$. Conversely, for any such tuple, take one basis vector per box, let each $B_i$ move a box one unit in direction $i$ and send it to zero when the next box is absent, let $I$ send the $\alpha$th framing vector to the origin box of $Y_\alpha$ when nonempty, and set $J=0$. Downward closure makes the shifts commute, the moment equation holds, and every box is generated from its origin. These data are stable and recover the given diagrams. The construction and recovery are inverse on gauge orbits, proving the fixed-point bijection.

Bring each torus-transformed representative back to the fixed representative by the inverse unique gauge lift from step 5.1. The variations then transform as $t_i\operatorname{End}(V)$ for $\dot B_i$, as $V^\vee\mathbf W^\vee$ for $\dot I$, and as $t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V$ for $\dot J$; the complex-equation target transforms as $t_1t_2\operatorname{End}(V)$. Thus the torus representations in the complex of step 1.1 are $C^0=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}$, $C^1=(t_1+t_2)\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}$, and $C^2=t_1t_2\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}$. Exactness at $C^0$ and $C^2$ follows from steps 2.1 and 3.1, so the tangent character is $[C^1]-[C^0]-[C^2]$, which is precisely the expression in the Statement.

The label set in step 6.1 is finite: for $k>0$ every box of a size-at-most-$k$ downward-closed diagram has both coordinates less than $k$, so the possible tuples lie in a finite collection of subsets; $k=0$ has only the empty tuple. Hence the fixed locus is a finite set in the Hausdorff quotient from [F3], and each point is isolated. By [F3] the quotient has a finite invariant affine atlas with algebraic action of $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^{N+2}$. In each slice its coordinate functions are eigenfunctions. A point fixed by the compact torus has every nonzero-weight coordinate equal to zero, since each nontrivial integer character is nontrivial on that compact torus; conversely these equations make the point fixed by $T_{\mathbb C}$. Thus the two fixed loci have the same point set. The fixed subscheme is smooth by [F4], because $T_{\mathbb C}$ is diagonalizable and hence linearly reductive. Its fixed ideal in these affine coordinates is generated by the nonzero-weight coordinates. Linearizing that ideal, using the tangent-kernel description in [F4], identifies its tangent with the invariant tangent subspace. A smooth fixed scheme with a finite point set has dimension zero at every point, so that subspace is zero. Therefore every complex tangent weight is a nonzero character. Its associated $u_\chi$ is a nonzero integer linear polynomial in the algebraically independent variables and is invertible in $K$. The tangent has complex dimension $2kN$, so the Euler product has exactly $2kN$ factors counted with multiplicity.

For each fixed $k$, there are finitely many partitions of $k$, hence finitely many $N$-tuples of total size $k$; every summand $E_{\vec Y}^{-1}$ is in $K$ by step 7.1. Therefore the coefficient is a finite sum and the sequence of coefficients defines the formal power series $Z_N^{\mathrm{fp}}(q)\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle$. At $k=0$, $V=0$, the empty tuple is the unique fixed point, the Euler product is empty and equals $1$, so the constant coefficient is $1$.

Assume full AC. Fix integers $N\geq1$ and $k\geq0$ and a positive real stability parameter $\zeta$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ have their standard Hermitian structures. Define $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ to be the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of data $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$, $J\in\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, and $\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ w\in W\}=V$. The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ in algebraically independent variables. For $\chi=t_1^{m_1}t_2^{m_2}\prod_\alpha e_\alpha^{n_\alpha}$ set $u_\chi=m_1\epsilon_1+m_2\epsilon_2+\sum_\alpha n_\alpha a_\alpha$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. For an $N$-tuple $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ set $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$, and

$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$

$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

A framed $U(N)$ connection is a smooth unitary connection $A$ on a Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle $E\to S^4$, together with a chosen unitary frame $\Phi:E_\infty\to\mathbb C^N$ of its fiber at $\infty$. Set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ and $F_A^-=(F_A-*_gF_A)/2$; the anti-self-dual condition is $F_A^+=0$, and the self-dual condition is $F_A^-=0$.

Let $\mathfrak u(N)$ be the anti-Hermitian matrices and put $B_N(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_N(XY)$. In the trace convention of the library, the charge of $A$ is $q_N(A)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$, and the positive anti-self-dual instanton number is $k(A)=-q_N(A)$. For $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$, the framed anti-self-dual charge-$k$ moduli set $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ consists of framed pairs $(E,A)$ with $F_A^+=0$ and $k(A)=k$, modulo the stated based gauge transformations. The integer-charge condition is part of the selected bundle sector; no analytic existence or uniqueness assertion is included in this definition. The trace and Hodge conventions agree with the supplied compact-four-manifold definition of $q_B$; its special $SU(2)$ integrality clause is not used to assert $U(N)$ integrality.

For $k\geq0$, take Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$. The ADHM data are
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V),\qquad I\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V),\qquad J\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W).$$
Their data space is $\mathcal R_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)$, and their complex and real moment-map expressions are

$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ i_j\in\{1,2\},\ w\in W\}=V,$$

The group $GL(V)$ consists of invertible complex-linear endomorphisms, and $U(V)$ is its subgroup preserving the chosen Hermitian inner product. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. For $\zeta>0$, the stable complex ADHM quotient $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{GIT},\zeta}_{k,N}$ is the geometric quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $GL(V)$ in the positive stability chamber; $\zeta$ labels that chamber and is not an additional coordinate on the complex equation set.

For a real parameter $\zeta\geq0$, the real moment-map presentation is the quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta\,\mathrm{id}_V,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $U(V)$. At $\zeta>0$ this is called the resolved or positive-FI ADHM quotient; at $\zeta=0$ its affine completion includes the small-instanton locus. The equations and quotient are definitions; this item does not assert that the real moment-map quotient is isomorphic to the stable complex quotient or to an instanton moduli space.

Write $\mathbb{CP}^2$ for the complex projective plane, $\ell_\infty=\{[0:z_1:z_2]\}$ for its line at infinity, and $\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for the sheaf of holomorphic functions on that line. The affine chart $\mathbb{CP}^2\setminus\ell_\infty$ is $\mathbb C^2$; projective compactification adds the whole line $\ell_\infty$, unlike the one-point compactification $S^4$. Let $\mathcal O(1)$ be the hyperplane line bundle and $\mathcal O(m)=\mathcal O(1)^{\otimes m}$ for $m\geq0$. A coherent sheaf is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$-modules that is locally finitely presented; it is torsion-free when no nonzero local section is annihilated by a nonzero local function. Its rank is the dimension of its generic fiber over the function field. Define its Hilbert polynomial by $P_E(m)=\sum_{i=0}^2(-1)^i\dim_{\mathbb C}H^i(\mathbb{CP}^2,E\otimes\mathcal O(m))$ for all sufficiently large integers $m$. The framed Gieseker moduli space $\mathcal G_{k,N}$ is the moduli of pairs $(E,\Phi)$ with $E$ a rank-$N$ torsion-free coherent sheaf, $P_E(m)=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and $\Phi:E|_{\ell_\infty}\cong\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}^{\oplus N}$. Its locally-free locus is distinguished from the boundary of non-locally-free sheaves. The Uhlenbeck set-theoretic compactification is the disjoint union of strata $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k-\ell,N}\times\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)$ for $0\leq\ell\leq k$, where $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)=(\mathbb R^4)^\ell/S_\ell$ records ideal point defects. The Gieseker space and the Uhlenbeck space are distinct: the former retains torsion-free sheaf data at the small-instanton boundary, while the latter records only ideal points. No compactness of either full space is asserted here.

Write $z_1=x^1+ix^2$ and $z_2=x^3+ix^4$. The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times T_G$, with $T_G\subset U(W)$ the diagonal framing torus, acts on ADHM data by
$$(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
This convention makes $\mu_{\mathbb C}$ transform with character $t_1t_2$ and leaves $\mu_{\mathbb R}$ invariant. Let $e_\alpha$ denote the character of the dual of the $\alpha$th framing line, so the framing representation has character $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. For the rotation characters write $t_1,t_2$, and write $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$ for their additive equivariant weights.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$, let
$S=k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be graded by total degree with $\deg x_i=1$, let
$\mathbb P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}S$ with twisting sheaves
$\mathcal O(d)=\widetilde{S(d)}$, and let $F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}$-module. Then there is a finitely generated graded
$S$-module $M$ with $\widetilde M\cong F$ and an exact sequence of graded
$S$-modules with degree-preserving maps
$$0\longrightarrow F_{n+1}\longrightarrow F_n\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow 0$$
in which every $F_i$ is a finite direct sum of shifted free modules $S(d)$
with $d\in\mathbb Z$, and whose sheafification
$$0\longrightarrow\widetilde F_{n+1}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\widetilde F_0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow 0$$
is an exact sequence of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}$-modules in which every
$\widetilde F_i$ is a finite direct sum $\bigoplus_j\mathcal O(d_{ij})$ of
twisting sheaves. The resolution has length at most $n+1$: the displayed free
terms $F_0,\dots,F_{n+1}$ are finite direct sums of shifted free modules, any
of them may be zero, a shorter resolution is allowed when it terminates
earlier, and the truncation degree of $M$ is chosen so that $M$ is finitely
generated and $\widetilde M\cong F$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring with $1$,
let $X$ be a scheme projective over $A$ in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention ([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]]): the structure
morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ factors as a closed immersion
$X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_A$ followed by the projection, for some $N\ge0$
([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]]). Let $L$ be an ample
invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-ample-invertible-sheaf]],
[[def-invertible-sheaf]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then there is an
integer $m_0$ such that
$$H^q\bigl(X,\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L^{\otimes m}\bigr)=0$$
for every $q>0$ and every integer $m\ge m_0$, with a single bound $m_0$
working simultaneously for all $q$; here $H^q$ is sheaf cohomology
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) and $L^{\otimes m}$ is the
$m$-fold tensor power ([[def-twist-quasi-coherent-sheaf-projective]]). The
empty scheme $X$, the empty base $\operatorname{Spec}A=\varnothing$, the zero
ring $A=0$, the zero module $\mathcal F=0$ and the case of an ample $L$ with
$\mathcal O(1)$ already very ample for a power $L^{\otimes d}$ with $d=1$ are
included. No effectivity of $m_0$ is claimed.

Let
$$\cdots \to A_{n-1} \to A_n \to A_{n+1} \to A_{n+2} \to A_{n+3} \to \cdots$$
and
$$\cdots \to B_{n-1} \to B_n \to B_{n+1} \to B_{n+2} \to B_{n+3} \to \cdots$$
be long exact sequences in an abelian category, together with a morphism of
these sequences. If the four comparison maps at $A_{n-1},A_n,A_{n+2},A_{n+3}$
are isomorphisms, then the comparison map $A_{n+1} \to B_{n+1}$ is an
isomorphism.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, and let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space. Then
the abelian category $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules has
enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module embeds into an injective
$\mathcal O_X$-module, and the functorial injective embedding supplied by the
Grothendieck injective-embedding theorem for Grothendieck categories supplies,
by iteration of cokernels, one specific injective resolution
$$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots$$
to each $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with no further selection
([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]). The Axiom of Choice
enters exactly through that embedding theorem applied to
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$; the category-theoretic verification below is
choice-free.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $X$ be a topological space and let
$\mathcal F$ be a flasque sheaf of abelian groups on $X$
([[def-flasque-sheaf]]). Then for every open subspace $U\subseteq X$ and every
integer $q>0$,
$$H^q(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0,$$
where $H^q(U,-)$ denotes sheaf cohomology on the space $U$
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) computed with the global
sections functor of $U$, and $\mathcal F|_U$ is the restriction of $\mathcal F$
to $U$. Equivalently, every restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ is $\Gamma$-acyclic
([[def-acyclic-sheaf-global-sections]]).

Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $I$ be a supplied injective resolution datum on a class $\mathcal D$, let
$F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor, and let
$$0\to A\to J^0\to J^1\to J^2\to\cdots$$
be an $F$-acyclic resolution of $A$ relative to $I$. Assume moreover that
$A\in\mathcal D$ and that, for $Z^0:=A$ and
$$0\to Z^q\to J^q\to Z^{q+1}\to0\qquad(q\ge0),$$
each $Z^q$ lies in $\mathcal D$. Then for every $n\ge 0$ there is a canonical
isomorphism
$$R_I^nF(A)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(F(J^\bullet_{\mathrm{del}})).$$

Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on a
topological space $X$, and let $I$ be the **presheaf image**
$$I(U):=\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))\subseteq\mathcal G(U).$$
Define the **image sheaf** $J$ by
$$ J(U):=\left\{\,t\in\mathcal G(U): \text{ for every }x\in U\text{ there exists }x\in V\subseteq U \text{ and }s\in\mathcal F(V)\text{ with }\varphi_V(s)=t|_V\,\right\}. $$
Then $J$ is a subsheaf of $\mathcal G$, $\varphi$ factors through $J$, and the
canonical map
$$aI\longrightarrow J$$
is an isomorphism. In particular, the image sheaf is the sheafification of the
objectwise image presheaf.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$, let
$\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to a\mathcal F$ be its sheafification map, and let
$\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $X$. Then every morphism of presheaves
$$\varphi:\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal G$$
factors uniquely through $\eta_{\mathcal F}$:
there is a unique morphism of sheaves
$$\overline\varphi:a\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal G$$
such that
$$\varphi=\overline\varphi\circ\eta_{\mathcal F}.$$

Let $(f,f^\sharp):(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces and let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-module-on-ringed-space]]). The direct image presheaf
$f_*\mathcal F$ is defined on opens $V\subseteq Y$ by
$(f_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V))$
([[def-direct-image-sheaf]]); when $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of modules, this
presheaf is again a sheaf of modules on $Y$
([[lem-direct-image-is-sheaf]]), and for a morphism of ringed spaces it is an
$\mathcal O_Y$-module, because $f_*$ is right adjoint to the inverse image
functor $f^*$ on modules ([[thm-pullback-pushforward-module-adjunction]]); a
right adjoint is left exact and additive
([[cor-a-right-adjoint-is-left-exact-and-a-left-adjoint-is-right-exact]]).

Fix the supplied functorial injective resolution datum $I$ on
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every
$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots$
([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]) with deleted complex
$I(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}}$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]). For
every $q\in\mathbb Z$ define the **$q$-th higher direct image sheaf**

$$R^qf_*\mathcal F:=R_I^qf_*(\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(f_*I(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}}\bigr),$$

the $q$-th right derived object of the additive left exact functor
$f_*:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ relative to the
fixed datum $I$ ([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]),
the cohomology object being taken in the abelian category of
$\mathcal O_Y$-modules. We also keep the convention $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ for
$q<0$.

By the derived-object convention this makes $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ a specific
$\mathcal O_Y$-module for every $\mathcal F$ and $q$, depending on the fixed
datum $I$; in degree zero the left exactness of $f_*$ supplies a canonical
natural isomorphism $R^0f_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*\mathcal F$
([[thm-zero-th-right-derived-functor-of-a-left-exact-functor-recovers-the-functor]],
which assumes the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-dependent-choice]])), so the $q=0$ term is the ordinary direct image.
The Axiom of Choice supplies the functorial injective resolution datum of
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and implies the
Dependent Choice required by the cited degree-zero and comparison theorems
([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). If $J$ is any other supplied injective resolution
datum on $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, then the functors $R_I^qf_*$ and
$R_J^qf_*$ are naturally isomorphic
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]]),
so the higher direct image is independent of the resolution up to a canonical
comparison isomorphism.

derivations.claim: Flatness of the local analytic-ring extension in [A1] makes analytification exact: tensoring an exact coherent stalk sequence with the holomorphic local ring preserves its kernels and cokernels. It also gives $(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G)^{an}\cong\mathcal F^{an}\otimes\mathcal G^{an}$ by associativity of stalkwise tensor product. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the same stalkwise tensor construction along its local defining ideal, so analytification commutes with that restriction.

For $\mathcal O_X$, both zeroth cohomology groups are $\mathbb C$ and higher algebraic cohomology vanishes by [F3]; higher analytic cohomology vanishes by the projective structure-sheaf clause of [A1]. For every integer $m$, the hyperplane sequence $0\to\mathcal O_X(m-1)\to\mathcal O_X(m)\to\mathcal O_{L}(m)\to0$ is exact on both sides by step 1.1. Induction on dimension for $L\cong\mathbb P^{n-1}$, followed by the long exact sequences and [F4], propagates the algebraic-to-analytic cohomology isomorphism from $m=0$ in both directions to every integer $m$. This proves comparison for every twisting line bundle.

Resolve a coherent algebraic $\mathcal F$ by the finite line-bundle resolution of [F2]. AC is retained through this finite-resolution supplier [F1]. By step 1.1 its analytification remains exact. Apply the cohomology comparison from step 2.1 to every term. Starting at the leftmost nonzero resolution term and using the long exact cohomology sequences, induction on the finite resolution length proves $H^q(X,\mathcal F)\cong H^q(X^{an},\mathcal F^{an})$ for every $q$. Thus the analytification functor is fully cohomology-compatible on coherent objects.

For coherent algebraic $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, the sheaf $\mathcal H om(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is coherent. Flatness in [A1] identifies its analytification with $\mathcal H om(\mathcal F^{an},\mathcal G^{an})$ stalkwise. Step 3.1 in degree zero therefore identifies algebraic and holomorphic morphisms. A finite locally free resolution of $\mathcal F$ computes $\operatorname{Ext}^q(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ by the hypercohomology of its Hom complex; exact analytification and termwise cohomology comparison identify the two finite Ext groups.

To see essential surjectivity, let $\mathcal M$ be holomorphic coherent. The uniform positive-twist generation assertion included in [A1] supplies one integer $a$ and finitely many global generators of $\mathcal M(a)$, hence a surjection $\mathcal O(-a)^r\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal M$. Its kernel is coherent. Applying the same assertion to the kernel gives a surjection from a finite sum of twisting sheaves; composing it with the kernel inclusion yields a finite presentation by twisting sheaves. The matrix entries are holomorphic sections of line bundles; step 2.1 identifies each such section with an algebraic section, so the presentation matrix is algebraic. Its algebraic cokernel $\mathcal F$ analytifies to $\mathcal M$ by exactness in step 1.1. If two algebraic sheaves analytify to isomorphic holomorphic sheaves, step 4.1 algebraizes that isomorphism and its inverse; their composites remain identities by faithfulness. This proves essential surjectivity and uniqueness up to algebraic isomorphism.

To complete the family comparison after the absolute equivalence of step 5.1, first establish the local-section formula: for any morphism of ringed spaces $f:Y\to B$ and module sheaf $M$, take the module-injective resolution from [F5]. Each term is flasque, its restriction to $f^{-1}U$ is flasque for every open $U\subset B$, and hence its sections there compute $H^q(f^{-1}U,M)$ by the acyclic-resolution theorem. The cohomology sheaf of $f_*I^\bullet$ is the sheafification of its presheaf cohomology: kernels are computed on opens, image sheaves are the sheafifications of presheaf images, and the assertion follows on stalks by exactness of filtered colimits. Thus $R^qf_*M=(U\mapsto H^q(f^{-1}U,M))^\#$, compatibly with restrictions and scalar multiplication. This argument covers analytic ringed spaces as well as schemes.

Write $Y=X\times S$ and let $\eta_Y:Y^{an}\to Y$, $\eta_S:S^{an}\to S$ be analytification maps. For every algebraic open $U\subset S$, [F6] gives $H^q(p^{-1}U,\mathcal E)\to H^q((p^{an})^{-1}\eta_S^{-1}U,\mathcal E^{an})$. Composing with the presheaf-to-sheaf map of step 6.1, then sheafifying on $S$, gives the $\mathcal O_S$-linear map $R^qp_*\mathcal E\to\eta_{S*}R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$. Pull back and tensor with $\mathcal O_{S^{an}}$ to obtain $c_q:(R^qp_*\mathcal E)^{an}\to R^qp^{an}_*\mathcal E^{an}$; explicitly $a\otimes[\xi]$ maps to $a$ times the analytically pulled-back germ of $\xi$. Tensor balancing proves well-definedness. This constructs an actual comparison morphism without assuming its invertibility or a relative-GAGA theorem.

At $t\in S^{an}$ over the closed complex point $s\in S$, tensor associativity gives $(M^{an})(t)=M(s)$ for every algebraic module sheaf $M$, and $\mathcal E^{an}|_{X^{an}\times\{t\}}=(\mathcal E_s)^{an}$. These are underived restrictions, valid also for singular or nonreduced bases. The square with top map $c_q(t)$, vertical maps the assumed algebraic and analytic fiber-base-change maps, and bottom map $H^q(X,\mathcal E_s)\to H^q(X^{an},(\mathcal E_s)^{an})$ commutes: represent a stalk by a class on $p^{-1}U$ using step 6.1; both paths pull back that class along the same map from the analytic fiber, with identical tensor restriction of coefficients, so [F6] identifies them. The bottom map is an isomorphism by step 3.1, and both vertical maps are isomorphisms by the Statement's explicit hypotheses. Hence $c_q(t)$ is an isomorphism. Both sheaves compared by $c_q$ are finite locally free by those same hypotheses. Locally their ranks agree, and its matrix has determinant with nonzero residue at every $t$, hence a unit; the adjugate gives a local inverse. Therefore $c_q$ is an isomorphism.

For an algebraic finite-type base map $S'\to S$, apply the same class-pullback construction to the pulled-back family. Tensor associativity identifies its analytification with the analytic pullback family. The square of the two comparison morphisms and the algebraic and analytic base-change maps commutes, since all maps pull back the same local cohomology classes and [F6] respects compositions. Whenever both families satisfy the Statement's locally-free and fiber-base-change hypotheses, step 8.1 makes their comparison morphisms invertible, so it identifies their base-change maps. This proves the complete stated family range, including the closed-fiber maps, without asserting arbitrary analytic-family algebraization. Full AC is inherited through [F1] and the resolution construction [F5]. The unresolved absolute analytic package [A1] remains necessary to step 3.1; nothing here closes that separate gap.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard bases. Let $X$ be the stable locus in the complex ADHM equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, where $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$, and stability means that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$. The action $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ of $GL(V)$ on $X$ is free and proper. Its orbit quotient with quotient topology is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension $2kN$, with tangent space $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$ for the infinitesimal ADHM deformation maps.

For $k>0$, a word frame $C(x)$ is a matrix whose columns are $k$ fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard framing basis vectors. The opens $U_C=\{x:\det C(x)\ne0\}$ cover $X$; words of length at most $k-1$ suffice. Each slice $S_C=\{x\in U_C:C(x)=I_V\}$ gives quotient coordinates, with $GL(V)\times S_C\to U_C$ a biholomorphism. Slice changes are holomorphic, in fact given by matrix inversion and polynomial operations on their domains. The quotient is also a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite $T$-invariant affine atlas of these slices, and the map from $X$ is a geometric quotient in the regular-function sense.

Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, with $h$ acting on the $\alpha$th standard framing vector by $e_\alpha^{-1}$. This descends to a smooth holomorphic action. At any fixed quotient point represented by $x$, there is a unique $g(t)\in GL(V)$ with $t\cdot x=g(t)\cdot x$. If column $\ell$ of $C(x)$ uses framing color $\alpha_\ell$ and contains $a_\ell,b_\ell$ letters $B_1,B_2$, then

$$g(t)=C(x)\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})C(x)^{-1}.$$

Thus the lift is a smooth character representation, without assuming Zariski density or a GIT linearization theorem. For $k=0$ the quotient is a point and these matrices and tangent spaces have their empty-dimensional interpretations. No correspondence with a real moment-map quotient, sheaf moduli or ASD connections is asserted.

Assume AC. Let $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}\subset\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb C}$ and let $\mathcal E$ be an algebraic coherent sheaf (a locally finitely presented module over the structure sheaf) of generic rank $N\ge1$. Torsion-free means that no nonzero stalk element is annihilated by a nonzero local function. Suppose it has a framing, namely an isomorphism $\phi:\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{\sim}W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$ for $W=\mathbb C^N$, and Hilbert polynomial $\chi(\mathcal E(m))=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$ for $k\ge0$, where $\chi$ is the alternating sum of coherent-sheaf cohomology dimensions. Then $\mathcal E$ is locally free near $L_\infty$ and

$$H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^2(\mathcal E(-1))=H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0.$$

$$\dim H^1(\mathcal E(-1))=\dim H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=k,\qquad H^0(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=0,\qquad \dim H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=2k+N.$$
The diagonal on $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ has its length-two Koszul resolution from the regular rank-two section described in the proof. Its associated finite Beilinson hypercohomology complex, applied to $\mathcal E(-1)$ and twisted by $\mathcal O(1)$, is a monad

$$H^1(\mathcal E(-2))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)\otimes\mathcal O\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal E(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$$

whose only cohomology is $\mathcal E$ in the middle. For an algebraic family over a finite-type complex base, the same construction is a family of monads provided the sheaf is flat over the base, the displayed cohomology groups have the stated constant ranks, and the corresponding cohomology-and-base-change maps are isomorphisms.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$, let
$X=\mathbb P^n_k$ with dualizing line bundle $\omega_X=\mathcal O(-n-1)$ and
residue trace $t_X:H^n(X,\omega_X)\to k$
([[def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace]]), and let
$\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}$ be the global sheaf Ext of
[[def-sheaf-ext-for-coherent-modules]].

1. **(The pairing.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$, $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$
   and $\eta\in H^q(X,F)$ set
   $$\langle\alpha,\eta\rangle_F\;:=\;t_X\Bigl(\chi^n_{\omega_X}\bigl(\alpha\cdot\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)\bigr)\Bigr),$$
   where $\chi^q_F:\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X,F)$
   is the canonical isomorphism of
   [[lem-injective-modules-flasque-and-ext-of-structure-sheaf]],
   $\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$ is the corresponding class in
   $\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)$, and
   $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,\omega_X)$
   is the Yoneda product of
   $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$ with
   $\beta=\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$, i.e. composition
   $\alpha\circ\beta$ of derived morphisms under
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal O_X}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))}(-,-[\bullet])$
   ([[thm-ext-is-hom-in-the-derived-category]],
   [[prop-yoneda-product-is-composition-in-the-derived-category]]). This
   **Serre duality pairing** is $k$-bilinear and natural in $F$.

2. **(Perfectness.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ and every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ the pairing
   $$\langle-,-\rangle_F:\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\times H^q(X,F)\longrightarrow k$$
   is a perfect pairing of $k$-vector spaces, i.e. both adjoint maps
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^q(X,F)^\vee$ and
   $H^q(X,F)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)^\vee$ are
   isomorphisms.

The case $q=n$ of clause 2 is the classical statement that
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^n(X,F)^\vee$,
$\varphi\mapsto(\eta\mapsto t_X(H^n(\varphi)(\eta)))$, is an isomorphism, and
for $F=\mathcal O_X$ clause 2 recovers $H^{n-q}(X,\omega_X)\cong H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)^\vee$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.
The field $\mathbb C$ is algebraically closed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

For a nonzero Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ the following are equivalent: $R$ is regular; $\operatorname{pd}_Rk<\infty$; $\operatorname{gldim}R<\infty$; and every finite $R$-module has finite projective dimension. When these hold, $\operatorname{gldim}R=\operatorname{pd}_Rk=\dim R$. A nonzero finite module over regular local $R$ is maximal Cohen–Macaulay (depth $\dim R$) if and only if it is free.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of
Noetherian local rings, let $I\subsetneq R$ be an ideal, and let $M$ be a
finite $S$-module. If $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and the multiplication map
$$I\otimes_R M\longrightarrow M$$
is injective, then $M$ is flat over $R$. There is **no** assumption that
$M$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module.

derivations.claim: Direct multiplication gives $\beta\alpha=(-z_0B_2+z_2)(z_0B_1-z_1)+(z_0B_1-z_1)(z_0B_2-z_2)+z_0^2IJ=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$. The $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ cross terms cancel pairwise, and the $z_1z_2$ terms cancel. On $L_\infty$, $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ is injective at every point because $z_1,z_2$ are not simultaneously zero. Thus $\alpha$ has full rank generically; its sheaf kernel is a torsion subsheaf of the locally free source, and hence is zero.

Conversely, let $\mathcal E$ be a framed torsion-free sheaf with the stated Hilbert polynomial. The preceding Beilinson lemma constructs its monad, with terms $V_1\mathcal O(-1)$, $M\mathcal O$, and $V_2\mathcal O(1)$ of ranks $k,2k+N,k$. Its restriction to $L_\infty$ remains exact at the ends because $\mathcal E$ is locally free there. Put $K=\ker\beta|_{L_\infty}$. The sequence $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to W\mathcal O\to0$ splits since $\operatorname{Ext}^1(W\mathcal O,V_1\mathcal O(-1))=V_1\otimes W^*\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$.

At a point of $L_\infty$, $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,0)$ is onto. At an affine point $[1:u_1:u_2]$, failure of surjectivity would give a nonzero $\lambda\in V^*$ with $\lambda B_1=u_1\lambda$, $\lambda B_2=u_2\lambda$, and $\lambda I=0$. Then $\lambda$ annihilates every vector $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, contradicting stability. Hence $\beta$ is everywhere onto, so $K=\ker\beta$ is a vector bundle of rank $k+N$.

A fiber kernel of $\alpha$ over $[1:u_1:u_2]$ is a nonzero vector $v$ with $B_1v=u_1v$, $B_2v=u_2v$, and $Jv=0$. Each $u_i$ must be an eigenvalue of the fixed matrix $B_i$, so the rank-drop locus is contained in the finite product of the two finite spectra. Such a vector spans a common invariant line in $\ker J$, so costability fails. Conversely, if costability fails, choose a nonzero common invariant subspace $S\subseteq\ker J$. On $S$, the complex equation implies $[B_1,B_2]|_S=-IJ|_S=0$, so the restrictions commute. By [F6] they have a common eigenvector; its eigenvalues give an affine point where $\alpha$ has a fiber kernel. Therefore $\alpha$ has full fiber rank everywhere exactly for costable data.

The remaining line extension $0\to V_1\mathcal O(-1)\oplus W\mathcal O\to M\mathcal O\to V_2\mathcal O(1)\to0$ has class in $\operatorname{Hom}(V_2,V_1)\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$, since $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Twist by $\mathcal O(-1)$ and take cohomology. The connecting map $V_2\to V_1\otimes H^1(\mathcal O(-2))$ is an isomorphism: the adjacent groups $H^0(\mathcal O(-1))$ and $H^1(\mathcal O(-1))$ vanish, while $H^1(\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C$. Thus $V_2$ is identified with $V_1$ by this canonical extension class. Choosing a basis of $V_1$ and using the fixed framed basis of $W$ identifies $M=V\oplus V\oplus W$ and the line maps with the two Euler blocks in the Statement. Any other such choice differs by one simultaneous element of $GL(V)$.

The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{\alpha}K\to\mathcal E\to0$ has locally free first two terms. Away from the finite rank-drop set of step 2.2, $\mathcal E$ is locally free; hence any torsion is supported at finitely many points. At such a point, the local ring is regular of dimension two and this sequence gives $\operatorname{pd}\mathcal E\le1$. The Auslander–Buchsbaum formula [F7] gives $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal E\ge1$. A nonzero finite-length torsion submodule would force depth zero, so no such torsion exists. Thus $\mathcal E$ is torsion-free of rank $(2k+N)-k-k=N$. The rank drops only off $L_\infty$, so $\mathcal E$ is locally free near the framing line.

The remaining coefficients of the two linear maps are their $z_0$ coefficients, so write $\alpha=(z_0B_1-z_1,z_0B_2-z_2,z_0J)^T$ and $\beta=(-z_0C_1+z_2,z_0C_2-z_1,z_0I)$. The coefficients of $z_0z_1$ and $z_0z_2$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ force $C_1=B_2$ and $C_2=B_1$; the $z_0^2$ coefficient is then $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. This recovers the stated ADHM form. The surjectivity of $\beta$ implies stability: if $U=\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(W)\}$ were proper, it is invariant and the induced $B_1,B_2$ on $V/U$ commute because $[B_1,B_2]=-IJ$ has image in $U$. Their dual actions on the nonzero annihilator $U^\perp\subset V^*$ commute, so [F6] gives a common eigen-covector $\lambda\ne0$ with $\lambda I=0$. At the corresponding affine point, $\lambda\beta=0$, contradicting surjectivity.

On $L_\infty$, the complex is $0\to V\mathcal O_{L_\infty}(-1)\xrightarrow{(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T}(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{(z_2,-z_1,0)}V\mathcal O_{L_\infty}(1)\to0$. The first two $V$ summands form the Euler resolution of the zero sheaf on the line, while the $W$ summand passes unchanged to middle cohomology. The framing is therefore the canonical identification $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}=W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. In the Grothendieck group, the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=[(V\oplus V\oplus W)\mathcal O]-[V\mathcal O(-1)]-[V\mathcal O(1)]$. Taking Euler characteristics after twisting by $\mathcal O(m)$ and using $\chi(\mathcal O(d))=\binom{d+2}{2}$ yields $\chi(\mathcal E(m))=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$.

The Beilinson construction is natural under framed sheaf isomorphisms, so an isomorphism of framed sheaves induces maps on the cohomology vector spaces used in steps 1.2–6.2 and hence a single change of basis $g\in GL(V)$; the normalized Euler blocks force the recovered tuples to differ by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)$. Conversely such a $g$ is an isomorphism of monads acting trivially on $W$, and therefore induces a framed sheaf isomorphism. This proves the pointwise inverse equivalence modulo $GL(V)$. For a finite-type data family, step 2.1 makes $\beta$ surjective on the total space, so $K=\ker\beta$ is locally free. The sequence $0\to V\mathcal O(-1)\to K\to\mathcal E\to0$ is exact and its terms before $\mathcal E$ are flat over the base. After tensoring with any residue field of the base, the first map remains sheaf-injective by step 1.1; hence $\operatorname{Tor}_1(k(s),\mathcal E)=0$. Since $\mathcal E$ is finite over each local ring of $\mathbb P^2\times S$ and its residue fiber is a vector space over the residue field, [F8] gives flatness over $S$. Under the stated relative cohomology and base-change hypotheses, the same constructions use vector bundles and are inverse for families.

Step 2.2 proves that costability is equivalent to fiberwise injectivity of $\alpha$. Since $\beta$ is surjective and $K$ is locally free, the quotient $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is locally free exactly when $\alpha$ has constant full rank; failure at any point gives a fiber dimension jump. Hence the locally-free sheaf locus is precisely the regular ADHM locus. Combining this with [F4] gives the positive-FI and zero-FI identifications in the Statement.

Apply the family equivalence to $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. A first-order deformation of the ADHM data is $(\dot B_1,\dot B_2,\dot I,\dot J)$ satisfying $d\mu_{\mathbb C}=0$; infinitesimal changes of basis are $d_0(\xi)=([\xi,B_1],[\xi,B_2],\xi I,-J\xi)$. Differentiating the monad gives the chain perturbation $(\dot\alpha,\dot\beta)$ with $\beta\dot\alpha+\dot\beta\alpha=0$, and a change by $d_0(\xi)$ is the corresponding chain homotopy. Since the family construction and its inverse commute with this dual-number base change, they induce inverse linear maps on first-order framed deformations and on the quotient tangent spaces $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$.

Let the rotation torus act on homogeneous coordinates with characters $1,t_1,t_2$, and let $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$ act on $W$. On the monad vector spaces choose characters $V(t_1t_2)^{-1}$ in the source, $Vt_2^{-1}\oplus Vt_1^{-1}\oplus Wh$ in the middle, and $V$ in the target, with the natural linearizations of $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(1)$. The first and second blocks are equivariant because the ratios of middle to source characters are respectively $t_1,t_2$; the $J$ block has ratio $t_1t_2h$; in $\beta$, the first two ratios are $t_2,t_1$ and the framing block ratio is $h^{-1}$. These are exactly the raw transformations in [F1]. On $L_\infty$ the Euler blocks cancel, leaving the framing factor $Wh$; its character is $\sum_a e_a^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_a e_a$. Thus the monad correspondence is torus-equivariant in the specified dual-framing convention.

If $k=0$, $V=0$, all four maps and both equations are the unique zero-dimensional maps, stability and costability are vacuous, and the monad is $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its middle cohomology is the framed bundle $W\mathcal O$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}$. Conversely, [F3] constructs this same zero-term monad from every framed sheaf with that polynomial, so the framing identifies each such sheaf with $W\mathcal O$.
